rows.assumption: A-1: The $70K increase measures what the offer is worth
A-2: The decision belongs to the engineer alone
A-3: Moving to California raises the household's state tax burden substantially
A-4: Engineer's current total comp is $200,000; partner earns $90,000; married filing jointly; standard deduction
A-5: The equity part of the $70K is worth 85–100% of face value in expectation
A-6: Comparable housing costs $18K–$36K/yr more in SF than Portland (central $27K)
A-7: Other living costs (sales tax, transport, groceries) add $4K–$12K/yr in SF (central $7K)
A-8: The partner can be re-employed in SF at equal pay within 0–12 months (central 6)
A-9: The offer's relocation requirement is non-negotiable
A-10: The SF employer's in-office requirement stays at 3 days/week
A-11: 2025/2026 federal, Oregon and California rate schedules hold over the decision horizon
A-12: Household taxable income = wages − $32,200 (no itemizing, no pre-tax deductions)
A-13: As Oregon residents super-commuting, Oregon credits the California tax on CA-sourced pay, so total state tax is about Oregon-level
A-14: The locked trade-off weights reflect the household's values
A-15: The current full-remote role remains available if the engineer stays
A-16: Leaving the current employer forfeits no material unvested equity or benefits
A-17: Job security at the new employer is comparable to the current one (no last-in-first-out exposure)
A-18: A large SF employer adds more career capital (scope, network, future pay) than the current role

chains.title: Relocating together raises household after-tax income by about $48,700, not $70,000, and state tax barely moves
On cash alone the relocation's steady-state household gain is about $14,700 a year, in a bracket that straddles zero
Relocating together carries a one-time cost of about $40,600 that the partner mostly bears, recovered in about 2.8 years centrally and never in the low case
The office requirement adds about 216 unpaid commuting hours a year that the status quo does not have
The composite (keep Portland, fly in three days a week) nets about $9,600 a year with the partner's career untouched, but exists only if the employer waives rel
The offer as structured (relocate together) ranks last of the four options, and no single weight change lifts it above staying
Between staying and the composite the choice turns on the employer's waiver and the engineer's own weights, so ask for the waiver before deciding and stay if it
For a household already in the 24% federal band, state income tax rates change the after-tax value of the raise by only about $490
Every way of taking the offer as written either ends the partner's current job or splits the household

conclusion.recommended: Do not accept the offer as structured — taking it as written ends the partner's current job or splits the household (chain C9), relocating the household ranks last of four options and no single weight change lifts it above staying (chain C6); before declining, ask the SF company in writing whether you can stay in Portland and fly in for the three office days, choose between that and staying on you

techniques_not_applied.reason: the question turns on a household's preferences and prices, not on whether a figure is a convention or a physical bound
no conclusion needs a law-permitted ceiling; every quantity is a price or a tax rate
the assumption space was enumerable directly and through inversion; no multi-causal effect needed explaining
the conclusion is a plan, so the pre-mortem was the Phase 5 technique
